findings.title: Success-criteria coverage and sequencing
findings.description:
Every functional and technical criterion in the slice design maps to a task:
- Slice-branch body: Tasks 7, 9 and 11.
- Unplanned repository with three no-input lines: 11.2.
- Merged-ancestor review excluded: 8.2.
- Base refusal and base source: Task 5, with the printed source in 13.1.
- Push preconditions: Task 6.
- Presence check with zero writes: Task 12.
- Title rules: Task 10a.
- Dry-run equality: 13.2.
- Timeout and transport matrix for five call sites: Task 14.
- Provider failure: 10.2.
- Import boundary: 15.1.
- Docstring correction: 15.2.
- Live creation: 16.2.

Tasks follow the design's implementation order, with no circular dependencies. Each test task directly follows its implementation task. I found no task without a criterion. Task 16.3 traces to the design's "refined at Phase 6" walkthrough note.

findings.title: Release step in Task 16.4 breaks two project rules
findings.description:
Task 16.4 has two problems:
- **Merge as a task item.** It lists "Merge `385-slice…` into `squadron-pr`". CLAUDE.md says never to write a merge or push as a task, sub-item or success criterion in a task file, and to merge only in Phase 7 after review passes. Remove the line.
- **Wait on the Project Manager.** It tells the implementer to "Ask the Project Manager how they want [code review] run". CLAUDE.md treats a step that waits on PM confirmation as invalid unless a named rule requires it. Replace it with a plain "code review required" line, or a `BLOCKED:` line if it truly cannot proceed.

findings.title: Identity check and local sha have no implementing task
findings.description:
Two inputs to the precondition stage are not built anywhere:
- **Operator identity.** The success criterion "adapter unable to identify the operator → exit non-zero, no write" is only wired by the ordering line in 13.1 ("identity, then pushed"). Task 6's `check_head_pushed` does not call `identify_operator`, and no task writes that call. Put it in `preconditions.py` with its own test case in 6.2, or name it explicitly in 13.1.
- **Local head sha.** `check_head_pushed` takes `local_sha`, but Task 3 adds only `current_branch` and `commits_in_range`, and nothing says where the sha comes from.
  - A near match exists: `resolve_reviewed_sha` (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py:143`) runs `git rev-parse HEAD`. It returns `None` and logs a warning on failure, which is the wrong contract for a precondition.
  - Add a helper that raises, or name the one to reuse and how its `None` is handled.

findings.title: The "model gets facts only" constraint has no test
findings.description:
The design's central rule is that the model receives `PrFacts` only, and is not asked for prose on no-input sections. Task 11.1 states the second half, but 11.2 only checks output text. It never asserts that:
- the fake composer was not invoked for a no-input section; or
- the prompt contains nothing beyond the facts.

No task states what the prompt contains either, although the design lists "the prompt" under body composition. Add one prompt-construction bullet to 11.1 and one assertion on the fake composer's received calls to 11.2.

findings.title: Provider failure in the title path is ambiguous
findings.description:
Two points are unclear:
- **Title composer failure.** Task 10 makes a provider exception a non-zero exit. Task 10a degrades empty, multi-line or over-length responses to the first commit subject. It does not say what happens when the title composer raises. Under D8 it should refuse, and a 10a.2 case would pin that down.
- **Where the exit lives.** 10.2 says the composer "exits non-zero", which implies `pr/body.py` raises `typer.Exit`. That couples the `pr/` package to Typer. Consider having the composer raise a typed error that the command in Task 13 maps to exit 1, and test it end to end in 13.2.

findings.title: Task 8 does not say how "newest in range" is decided
findings.description: Task 8.1 says to take the survivor whose sha is newest, but not how that is determined. `commits_in_range` from Task 3 already returns newest-first shas. Reusing that order avoids a second `git rev-list` call. Reviewed shas are full shas (`persistence.py:143` uses `git rev-parse HEAD`), so exact membership is safe.

findings.title: Task 4.2 adds little beyond 4.1
findings.description: The real criterion for 4.2 is that the existing `show` tests pass unchanged, which 4.1 already states. The only new test is `resolve_locator` returning the locator for each target form. Consider merging 4.2 into 4.1. Otherwise the task count is proportionate to a seven-module package plus a CLI command.

findings.title: No commit markers and no load tests
findings.description: The file has no `**Commit**:` markers, which is acceptable, so CLAUDE.md's per-top-level-task commit cadence applies. The slice states no NFR, so no `tests/load/` task or CI gating task is required.
